Must, Might, Could, May, and Can't to Speculate About the Present
You use the modals must, might, could, may and can't to speculate or make guesses about something in the present. The modal you choose depends on the level of probability you want to express.
She could be having mental health problems.
You use must for logical conclusions. There is a strong degree of certainty about the present situation.
You use may, might and could to speculate about things in the present when there are other possibilities or when the situation is possible but not certain. These modals have the same meaning.
You use can't when the situation is impossible.
Look at the chart for the use of modals to speculate about the present.

Will and Won't in the if-clause to express polite request or refusal

You use the first conditional to talk about possibilities in the present or future - things which might happen.
You use the if clause with Will and Won't to express polite request or refusal
A first conditional sentence consists of two clauses, an "if" clause and a main clause:
I'll come and meditate if I stop work before 5. = It's possible that I can meditate on the condition that I stop work before 5.
You sometimes use will and won't in the if-clause with the meanings of refusal (won't), polite request (will), or strong disapproval at someone's insistence on doing something (will):

Amy: Good to see you Vanessa. How was work?
Vanessa: Thanks! I am totally wiped out. Again. I'm really fed up with it! Today I felt like I was a therapist, a police officer, a nurse and a costume designer. First of all, I am worried about Rachel, who was off today. She hasn't been very team-oriented lately and she has been telling me some disturbing things, in confidentiality, of course. She could be having mental health problems. She needs help. I won't put up with it if she brings her issues into the dining room. In the morning, Michael sliced his hand open and I needed to bandage him up. Then Alexander tried to tell the homeless guy, Burt, to get off the front step and Burt, who's full of hate and discrimination, punched him! Somehow I managed to convince Burt to calm down and go sit somewhere else before things got even uglier. I also think Alexander may be in trouble with the police ... which is very irritating!
Oh, and one of the new servers was wearing this totally inappropriate shirt, so I had to talk to her about her appearance and fashion a new outfit out of clothing from the closet. It even required a bit of sewing, for God's sake! Meanwhile I was trying to be mindful and trying to communicate openly ... but honestly I think I've had enough with it!

Amy: It sounds like a lot to deal with. You must be worn out. If you have time will you join me for some meditation tomorrow night? You might want to keep as level-headed and calm as possible.
Vanessa: Yes. I'll come and meditate if I finish work before five. I should be able to leave at a reasonable time.
Amy: If you don't leave by five, I will come over there and force you to leave. Remember the work/life balance? If you won't take time for yourself, you'll have a nervous breakdown.

Vanessa: Yes. I know. Will you always remind me to keep calm if I appear to need reminding?
Amy: You can bet on it!
